source.title: High-entropy Advantage in Neural Networks' Generalizability
source.authors: Entao Yang; Xiaotian Zhang; Yue Shang; Ge Zhang

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including supplementary materials, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures entropy-conditioned test performance against SGD training, using a different method to investigate generalization. Its entropy findings do not directly test any of the eight listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test random-label fitting, compare convolutional and fully connected networks, evaluate the listed optimizer, batch-size, or dropout claims, measure magnitude-aware sharpness, or remove memorized examples. It reports entropy landscapes and width-dependent entropy advantages; cited prior work is not extracted as results.
record.test_reason: The study measures entropy-conditioned generalization, which none of V1–V8 names. It assumes SGD's generalization advantage when choosing a comparator, but does not test V4's optimizer comparison. Width sweeps measure the entropy advantage, without establishing interpolation thresholds or test-error trends past them.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: at matched training loss, high-entropy states generally generalize better than or comparably to optimizer-trained states, with larger advantages in narrower networks. The authors additionally propose parameter-space volume as an explanation for generalization and motivate entropy-seeking optimizers; these are interpretations, not direct tests of V1–V8.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Wang-Landau Monte Carlo or molecular dynamics to sample entropy-conditioned states and compares them with SGD (Adam for spiral regression); this is not the intervention or measurement in the listed claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported entropy advantage varies with network width and task; it diminishes with increased width in the tested sweeps. Spiral regression uses Adam because SGD performs much worse.

fits_no_version.finding: At matched training loss, entropy-conditioned states generally outperform SGD on the tested synthetic, housing, and image tasks; polymer-regression performance is better or comparable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: High-entropy parameter regions can have better held-out performance than optimizer-trained states at matched training loss in these tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: The entropy advantage generally shrinks with width, disappearing at width 1000 for spiral regression and becoming negligible in some housing and polymer settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The entropy-versus-optimizer performance gap depends on network width and task.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report that SGD performs much worse than Adam on spiral regression, motivating their use of Adam, without a quantified optimizer comparison.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adam can outperform SGD on this synthetic regression task.

record.problems: The study does not test random-label memorization or any of the listed versions directly. Several width comparisons are described qualitatively and their precise values are figure-only. The spiral regression width experiments use Adam because SGD performs much worse. For the ResNet CIFAR result, only a qualitative result is stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No results that bear on the eight specified versions were reported. Cited results from prior work and figure-only exact values were not extracted as independent rows.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance compared with natural-label training under the same recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width achieving zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, local connectivity, and convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under specified tuning regimes and recovery interventions.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on training-set size, strength, and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and ranking against other measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are relative to the listed versions, which these measures cannot determine. Entropy is not magnitude-aware sharpness. Overparameterization by parameter count does not establish interpolation. The entropy comparisons belong under fits_no_version rather than as evidence rows for V1–V8.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or same-recipe comparison of natural-label and random-label generalization.
Width sweeps compare the max-entropy and SGD curves, not test error across widths past the zero-training-error threshold.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks on images.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD on the listed benchmarks.
No large-batch versus small-batch generalization comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
Entropy is measured, but magnitude-aware sharpness is not measured or compared with generalization gaps.
No removal or retraining of memorized examples.

rows.subject: FNN (3 layers) × (6 neurons)
rows.operation_detail: Compared max-entropy equilibrium test accuracy with mean SGD test accuracy at matched training loss.

conditions.value: 6 independently generated training and testing datasets

rows.measure: Test accuracy at a given training loss
rows.value: Equilibrium accuracy supremacy over SGD accuracy for each given ln(Ltrain) when ln(Ltrain) reaches a low level [ln(Ltrain) ≈ −0.5].
rows.note: Authors state that equilibrium accuracy is higher at low training loss; they report the six-dataset average for WLMC.
rows.check: The entropy-versus-SGD comparison measures no listed version; observed describes the paper's own entropy finding.

rows.subject: FNNs, 4 sizes
rows.size_stated: Smallest: 116 trainable parameters; other sizes not stated here
rows.operation_detail: Compared max-entropy test accuracy with SGD test accuracy at the training loss reached at the end of SGD training.

conditions.value: 8 experiments across FNN sizes and two training times

rows.value: For all experiments, the training loss at the end of SGD training corresponds to an equilibrium test accuracy that outperforms the SGD accuracy with a large margin.
rows.note: Aggregate statement across the eight experiments; individual experiment values are shown in the figure.
rows.check: An aggregate entropy-versus-SGD comparison, without a listed-version outcome or an interpolation-threshold analysis.

rows.subject: 2-layer FNN, 20 hidden neurons
rows.operation_detail: Compared max-entropy test loss with SGD test loss at matched training loss.
rows.value: At a given Ltrain, the corresponding max entropy loss is clearly lower than the test loss obtained via SGD training.
rows.uncertainty: Standard errors smaller than the black curve’s width.
rows.locator: Results, Kaggle House Price Prediction; Figure 2(a)
rows.note: Regression task; comparison is at matched training loss.
rows.check: Measures entropy-conditioned regression loss against SGD, not any listed version. The supplementary protocol selects the lowest SGD test loss within training-loss bins when multiple results are available; the baseline needs this qualification.

rows.subject: CNN with 5 convolutional layers followed by one fully-connected layer
rows.operation_detail: Compared max-entropy test accuracy with mean SGD test accuracy at matched training loss.

conditions.value: Selected MNIST; 250 training and 250 test images

rows.value: For a given train loss, the corresponding max entropy accuracy generally outperforms the SGD training, especially when the train loss is small (ln(Ltrain) < −2).
rows.uncertainty: Standard error at each train-loss level smaller than the curve width.
rows.locator: Results, MNIST Image: Handwritten Digit Recognition; Figure 2(b)
rows.note: The authors also state the high-entropy band is around 0.1 test accuracy when training loss is high.
rows.check: Measures entropy-conditioned performance, not any listed version. The landscape uses smoothed test accuracy with alpha = 5, rather than ordinary accuracy.

rows.subject: 10-layer ResNet11
rows.operation_detail: Compared entropy-landscape test performance with SGD-trained performance.

conditions.value: Selected CIFAR-10; 2500 training and 2500 test images, deer or frog
Batch normalization replaced with layer normalization

rows.measure: Test performance (metric not stated in the text)
rows.value: The results ... exhibit strong high-entropy advantage.
rows.locator: Supplementary Materials, Entropy Advantage for ResNet on selected CIFAR dataset; Figure 6
rows.note: Metric values are presented in the figure; the text states the qualitative result.
rows.check: An entropy-versus-SGD comparison within one convolutional architecture does not test convolutional versus fully connected generalization.

rows.subject: TransPolymer regressor head, width 50
rows.operation_detail: Compared max-entropy test loss with SGD test loss at matched training loss.
rows.value: The corresponding max-entropy loss at each Ltrain is slightly lower or comparable to its SGD training analog.
rows.uncertainty: Standard error smaller than the curve width.
rows.locator: Results, Polymer SMILES: Language Modeling; Figure 2(c)
rows.note: The text characterizes the advantage as slight or comparable.
rows.check: Measures property-regression loss for a head on a frozen encoder, not a listed optimizer or language-model generalization comparison. Supplementary results describe width 50 as matching SGD.

rows.subject: FNNs, widths 30, 100, 300, and 1000
rows.operation_detail: Compared max-entropy and Adam-trained test performance across network widths.

conditions.value: 500 points, equally divided into training and test sets

rows.measure: Gap between max-entropy and Adam test performance
rows.value: The high-entropy advantage decreases as W increases, and finally fades away when W = 1000.
rows.locator: Results, Effect of Network Width; Figure 3
rows.note: The reported comparison concerns the entropy advantage, not the change in test error caused by widening.
rows.check: A shrinking entropy-versus-Adam gap does not establish V2's test-error trend beyond interpolation. The stated parameter counts are inconsistent with the description of two hidden layers; architecture and counts need reconciliation.

rows.subject: FNNs, widths 10, 20, 50, and 100
rows.operation_detail: Compared max-entropy and SGD test-loss curves across network widths.
rows.measure: Gap between max-entropy and SGD test loss
rows.value: The gap between the max-entropy curve and the SGD training curve becomes smaller (and almost disappeared at W = 100) with the increase of W.
rows.locator: Supplementary Materials, High Entropy Advantages Analysis; Kaggle House Price Prediction; Figure 7
rows.note: No width-specific test-loss values are stated in the text.
rows.check: Measures the entropy-versus-SGD gap across widths, without demonstrating zero training error or the test-error trend beyond that threshold.

rows.subject: CNNs, 2, 3, and 4 channels
rows.operation_detail: Compared max-entropy and SGD test-accuracy curves across channel counts.
rows.measure: Gap between max-entropy and SGD test accuracy
rows.value: CNNs with 3 and 4 channels present similar level of advantage, while the max-entropy state of the 2-channel CNN has clearly higher test accuracy when train loss is small.
rows.locator: Supplementary Materials, High Entropy Advantages Analysis; MNIST Digit Recognition; Figure 8
rows.note: The text compares the entropy advantage across channel counts.
rows.check: Measures entropy advantage across convolutional channel counts, not V2's fully connected width comparison or V3's architecture comparison.

rows.subject: TransPolymer regressor heads, widths 2, 10, 50, and 100
rows.operation_detail: Compared max-entropy and SGD test-loss curves across regressor-head widths.
rows.value: Max-entropy state is slightly better at W = 10; equally well with SGD training at all training losses for W = 50 and W = 100; larger gap at W = 2.
rows.uncertainty: Two independent experiments were run for W = 2.
rows.locator: Supplementary Materials, Polymer SMILES Language Modeling; Figures 9–10
rows.note: Authors state test R2 exceeded 0.9 for all four SGD-trained regressor heads.
rows.check: Combines larger, slight, and absent entropy advantages across widths; these are not one partial effect. None measures a listed version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
